title: I've been ripped off!
goal: At an electronics shop, the laptop you bought there last week keeps switching off; complain firmly but politely, and don't leave without an answer
tip: Complain in steps: what's wrong and since when (min awwal yōm), what you've tried (jarrabt kill shay), how you feel (aḥiss inni inghashshēt, ana mnarfaz), then what you want. If they hide behind 'policy', say what you see: aḥiss innak timāṭil, and don't leave until il-masʼūl has looked at it.
grammar: complaining: problem, feeling, demand (aḥiss inni inghashshēt, timāṭil)
dialogue: A
هلا، شو أقدر أسوي لك؟
hala, shu agdar asawwī-lak?
Hello, what can I do for you?
B
اشتريته منكم الأسبوع اللي طاف، وكل شوي يطفي
ishtarētah minkum il-usbūʿ illi ṭāf, w kill shwayy yiṭfi
(This laptop:) I bought it from you last week, and it keeps switching off.
A
يمكن من الشاحن. جربت شاحن ثاني، ولّا يبي فحص؟
yimkin min ish-shāḥin. jarrabt shāḥin thāni, walla yabi faḥiṣ?
Maybe it's the charger. Have you tried another charger, or does it need checking?
B
جربت كل شي. فيه عيب من أول يوم
jarrabt kill shay. fīh ʿēb min awwal yōm
I've tried everything. It's had a fault from day one.
A
زين، نطرشه للوكالة، وياخذ شي ثلاث أسابيع. هذي سياسة المحل
zēn, nṭarrshah lil-wakāla, w yākhidh shay thalāth asābīʿ. hādhi siyāsat il-maḥall
OK, we'll send it to the agent, and it'll take about three weeks. That's the shop's policy.
B
ثلاث أسابيع؟ مب معقول! أنا طفشان، أحس إني انغشيت
thalāth asābīʿ? mub maʿgūl! ana ṭafshān, aḥiss inni inghashshēt
Three weeks? No way! I'm sick of it; I feel I've been ripped off.
A
يا أخوي، اللابتوب عليه كفالة سنة، ما بتخسر شي
yā akhūy, il-lābtōb ʿalēh kafāla sana, ma bitikhsar shay
Brother, the laptop has a year's warranty; you won't lose anything.
B
الكفالة مب عشان أقعد بدون لابتوب. أنا منرفز، وأحس إنك تماطل
il-kafāla mub ʿashān agʿid bidūn lābtōb. ana mnarfaz, w aḥiss innak timāṭil
The warranty isn't there so I can sit without a laptop. I'm fed up, and I feel you're stalling.
A
لا والله. إذا طلع عيب مصنعي، المسؤول يعطيك واحد يديد اليوم
la wallāh. idha ṭilaʿ ʿēb maṣnaʿi, il-masʼūl yaʿṭīk wāḥid yidīd il-yōm
No, honestly. If it turns out to be a manufacturing fault, the manager will give you a new one today.
B
ما يخالف. أنا جاد، بتريا هني لين يشوفه
ma ykhālif. ana jādd, batrayya hni lēn yshūfah
Fine, no problem. I'm serious; I'll wait here till he looks at it.
items: a warranty, a guarantee (on something you buy)
fed up, irritated, on edge (a man)
you're stalling, you're putting (me) off (to a man)
to a woman: timāṭlīn (تماطلين); to a group: timāṭlūn (تماطلون)
a manufacturing fault, a factory defect

title: Ṣallū ʿala n-nabi, lads!
goal: At Thursday's five-a-side, Khalfān says your classmate Mājid fouled him on purpose; calm him down before it turns into a real fight
tip: Gulf speakers calm someone with religious formulas that need an answer: taʿawwadh min ish-shēṭān gets aʿūdh billāh min ish-shēṭān, and ṣallū ʿala n-nabi gets a blessing on the Prophet. Between friends, add rawwig 'chill', then turn it into a joke.
grammar: calming someone down: taʿawwadh min ish-shēṭān, ṣallū ʿala n-nabi, rawwig
dialogue: A
فاول! ماجد ضربني على ريولي، وهو متعمد!
fāwil! Mājid ẓarabni ʿala ryūli, w huwa mitʿammid!
Foul! Mājid kicked my legs, and he did it on purpose!
B
خلاص عاد يا خلفان، زودتها. روق، ما كان متعمد
khalāṣ ʿād yā Khalfān, zawwadt-ha. rawwig, ma kān mitʿammid
That's enough now, Khalfān, you've gone too far. Chill; he didn't do it on purpose.
A
كل مرة نفس الشي! هالمرة ما بسكت له
kill marra nafs ish-shay! hal-marra ma baskit lah
Every time it's the same! This time I won't let it go.
B
تعوذ من الشيطان. أدري إنك منرفز، بس عشان كورة ترفع صوتك؟
taʿawwadh min ish-shēṭān. adri innak mnarfaz, bas ʿashān kūra tirfaʿ ṣōtak?
Seek refuge from Satan. I know you're fed up, but you're raising your voice over football?
A
أعوذ بالله من الشيطان. بس صج، ريلي تعورني
aʿūdh billāh min ish-shēṭān. bas ṣij, rīli tʿawwirni
I seek refuge in God from Satan. But really, my leg hurts.
B
سلامات. ماجد، تعال. صلوا على النبي يا شباب
salāmāt. Mājid, taʿāl. ṣallū ʿala n-nabi yā shabāb
Hope you're OK. Mājid, come here. Calm down, lads; say a blessing on the Prophet.
A
اللهم صل وسلم عليه. الله يسلمك. بس خله يعتذر
allāhumma ṣalli w sallim ʿalēh. allāh ysallmak. bas khallah yiʿtidhir
God bless him and grant him peace. Thanks. But he should apologise.
B
ماجد يقول حقك علي. والله ما تستاهل الزعل
Mājid ygūl ḥaggak ʿalay. wallāh ma tistāhil iz-zaʿal
Mājid says he's sorry. Honestly, it's not worth getting upset over.
A
زين، خلها تعدي هالمرة. بس قول له يخفف شوي
zēn, khallha tʿaddi hal-marra. bas gūl-lah ykhaffif shwayy
OK, I'll let it go this time. But tell him to take it easy.
B
يلا، سلموا على بعض ونكمل اللعب
yalla, sallmu ʿala baʿaẓ w nkammil il-liʿib
Come on, shake hands and let's get on with the game.
items: chill, calm down, take it easy (to a man) (friends only)
to a woman: rawwgi (روقي); to a group: rawwgu (روقوا)
calm down, don't let anger get you (lit. seek refuge from Satan) (to a man)
to a woman: taʿawwadhi (تعوذي); the reply is aʿūdh billāh min ish-shēṭān
I seek refuge in God from Satan (the reply: 'all right, I'm calming down')
calm down, everyone (lit. pray for the Prophet) (to a group)
to one man: ṣall ʿala n-nabi (صل على النبي); the reply blesses the Prophet: allāhumma ṣalli w sallim ʿalēh
let it go, let it pass (to a man)
to a woman: khallīha tʿaddi (خليها تعدي); (recognise)
culture: taʿawwadh min ish-shēṭān draws on a hadith: two men were quarrelling, and the Prophet said that if the angry one said aʿūdhu billāhi min ish-shayṭān, his anger would leave him. So the formula works as 'calm down', and saying the answer back is how the other person shows he is calming down.
task: This week: with a tutor or exchange partner, talk for 10 minutes about an argument you saw or had (real or made up) and who calmed it down. Then role-play: they get angry over something small, and you calm them as a friend (rawwig, taʿawwadh min ish-shēṭān, ma tistāhil iz-zaʿal). Then again as if they were an elder in a majlis: ṭāl ʿumrak, and no friends-only words.

title: It was an oversight on our part
goal: On the phone, apologise formally to a client for the file with the wrong figures you sent him yesterday, and say what you've done about it
tip: A formal apology names the mistake, owns it and promises care, with no excuses: il-khaṭaʼ min ʿindana, ma lah mubarrir, w binkūn ḥarīṣīn akthar. The other side often closes it with ḥaṣal khēr 'no harm done'.
grammar: a formal apology (formal): il-khaṭaʼ min ʿindana, ma lah mubarrir
dialogue: B
السلام عليكم طال عمرك، معاك سالم من الشركة
as-salāmu ʿalaykum ṭāl ʿumrak, maʿāk Sālim min ish-sharika
Hello, sir; it's Sālim from the company.
A
وعليكم السلام، هلا سالم. خير إن شاء الله؟
wa ʿalaykum is-salām, hala Sālim. khēr in shāʼ allāh?
Hello, Sālim. Is everything all right?
B
أبي أعتذر منك عن ملف أمس
abi aʿtadhir minnak ʿan malaff ams
I'd like to apologise to you for yesterday's file.
A
لاحظت، الأرقام كانت قديمة، وأنا عرضتها على الإدارة! قهرتني. منو المسؤول؟
lāḥaẓt, il-argām kānat gadīma, w ana ʿaraẓt-ha ʿala l-idāra! gahartni. minu l-masʼūl?
I noticed: the figures were old, and I'd shown them to the management! You've really annoyed me. Who's responsible?
B
أنا المسؤول. الخطأ من عندنا، وما له مبرر
ana l-masʼūl. il-khaṭaʼ min ʿindana, w ma lah mubarrir
I am. The mistake was ours, and there's no excuse for it. (formal)
A
زين إنك اتصلت. أدري إنه مب متعمد. الغلط يصير، بس الإهمال لا
zēn innak ittaṣalt. adri innah mub mitʿammid. il-ghalaṭ yṣīr, bas il-ihmāl la
Good that you called. I know it wasn't deliberate. Mistakes happen, but carelessness isn't acceptable.
B
معك حق. النسخة الصح في إيميلك، وراجعتها بنفسي، على مسؤوليتي
maʿak ḥagg. in-nuskha ṣ-ṣaḥḥ fi īmēlak, w rājaʿt-ha b-nafsi, ʿala masʼūliyyti
You're right. The right version is in your email; I checked it myself, on my responsibility.
A
ما يخالف. بس ما أبي هالشي يصير مرة ثانية
ma ykhālif. bas ma abi hash-shay yṣīr marra thānya
All right. But I don't want this to happen again.
B
ما بتتكرر إن شاء الله. من اليوم بنكون حريصين أكثر
ma bititkarrar in shāʼ allāh. min il-yōm binkūn ḥarīṣīn akthar
It won't happen again, God willing. From today we'll be more careful. (formal)
A
حصل خير يا ولدي. هفوة وتعدي، والمهم إنك اعترفت
ḥaṣal khēr yā wildi. hafwa w tʿaddi, w il-muhimm innak iʿtaraft
No harm done, son. A slip, and it'll pass; what matters is you owned up.
items: the mistake was ours, the error's on our side (formal)
there's no excuse for it, it can't be justified (formal)
one man: ḥarīṣ (حريص); one woman: ḥarīṣa (حريصة)
no harm done, it's all fine now (accepting an apology)

title: Cousins who won't speak
goal: In Bū Rāshid's majlis, he tells you a joke in the family group has set Rāshid against Ḥamad, the cousin whose wedding you went to; agree to be the go-between
tip: Mediating starts with naming the problem gently: mit-hāwshīn 'they've fallen out', kill wāḥid rākib rāsah 'each one's dug his heels in'. Then offer to step in (aṣalliḥ bēnhum) before il-fitna grows, and hear each side first: basmaʿ min Rāshid awwal.
grammar: mediating I: naming the quarrel, offering to step in (mit-hāwshīn, rākib rāsah)
dialogue: A
يا ولدي، أبيك في سالفة. راشد وحمد ولد أخوي متهاوشين
yā wildi, abīk fi sālfa. Rāshid w Ḥamad wild akhūy mit-hāwshīn
Son, I need you for something. Rāshid and my brother's son Ḥamad have fallen out.
B
أفا يا عمي! حمد المعرس؟ شو صار بينهم؟
afa yā ʿammi! Ḥamad il-miʿris? shu ṣār bēnhum?
Oh no, uncle! Ḥamad, the groom? What happened between them?
A
حمد حط في قروب الأهل مقطع لراشد وهو طايح، وراشد رد عليه بكلام ما يصير
Ḥamad ḥaṭṭ fi grūb il-ahal magṭaʿ l-Rāshid w huwa ṭāyiḥ, w Rāshid radd ʿalēh b-kalām ma yṣīr
Ḥamad put a clip of Rāshid falling over in the family group, and Rāshid answered him with words he shouldn't have used.
B
عشان مقطع؟ مزحة سخيفة، بس يمكن حمد ما كان متعمد
ʿashān magṭaʿ? mazḥa sakhīfa, bas yimkin Ḥamad ma kān mitʿammid
Over a clip? A silly joke, but maybe Ḥamad didn't mean it.
A
يمكن، بس بو حمد زعل. قلت له تعوذ من الشيطان، بس يقول راشد ما احترم ولده
yimkin, bas Bū Ḥamad ziʿal. gilt-lah taʿawwadh min ish-shēṭān, bas ygūl Rāshid ma iḥtaram wildah
Maybe, but Ḥamad's father got upset. I told him to calm down, but he says Rāshid didn't respect his son.
B
يعني صارت سالفة كبار، وكل واحد راكب راسه؟
yaʿni ṣārat sālfat kbār, w kill wāḥid rākib rāsah?
So it's become a grown-ups' matter, and each one's dug his heels in?
A
هيه. وأنا إذا دخلت، تصير بيني وبين أخوي، وتكبر الفتنة. وانت ربيعهم الثنين
hē. w ana idha dakhalt, tṣīr bēni w bēn akhūy, w tikbar il-fitna. w inta rbīʿhum ith-thnēn
Yes. And if I step in, it becomes between me and my brother, and the bad blood grows. And you're friends with both of them.
B
أبشر يا عمي. بسمع من راشد أول، وبعدين أكلم حمد
abshir yā ʿammi. basmaʿ min Rāshid awwal, w baʿdēn akallim Ḥamad
Consider it done, uncle. I'll hear Rāshid out first, and then talk to Ḥamad.
A
زين تسوي. ترا هذي صلة الرحم، والصلح خير، وخيرهم اللي يبدا بالسلام
zēn tsawwi. tara hādhi ṣilat ir-raḥim, w iṣ-ṣulḥ khēr, w khērhum illi yibda bis-salām
Good. These are family ties, mind; making peace is best, and the better of the two is the one who greets first.
B
إن شاء الله أصلح بينهم، ويفتحون صفحة يديدة
in shāʼ allāh aṣalliḥ bēnhum, w yiftaḥūn ṣafḥa yidīda
God willing I'll make peace between them, and they'll make a fresh start.
items: they've fallen out, they're quarrelling (two or more people)
one man: mit-hāwish (متهاوش); one woman: mit-hāwsha (متهاوشة)
he's dug his heels in, he won't back down (lit. riding his head)
trouble, bad blood (stirred up between people)
keeping up family ties (a religious duty)
making peace is best (a saying from the Qurʼan)
culture: iṣ-ṣulḥ khēr, 'making peace is best', echoes the Qurʼan (4:128, wa ṣ-ṣulḥu khayr). khērhum illi yibda bis-salām echoes a hadith: a Muslim shouldn't cut off his brother for more than three days, and the better of the two is the one who greets first. ṣilat ir-raḥim, keeping up ties with relatives, is a religious duty, so a family quarrel is everyone's business.

title: You hurt his feelings
goal: At a karak stand, talk to Ḥamad, the cousin whose wedding you went to, about the family-group row; give Rāshid's side, hear his, and get him to move first
tip: As the go-between, give each side's feelings, not your verdict: Rāshid infaẓaḥ, kasart khāṭrah. Answer the fear behind a question (ḥāgid ʿalay?) with la, galbah abyaẓ, call it ṣār sūʼ fahm, and ask for one small step: ibda inta.
grammar: mediating II: giving each side's feelings (kasart khāṭrah, galbah abyaẓ, ṣār sūʼ fahm)
dialogue: B
حمد، عندك دقيقة؟ أبي أكلمك عن راشد
Ḥamad, ʿindak dagīga? abi akallmak ʿan Rāshid
Ḥamad, have you got a minute? I want to talk to you about Rāshid.
A
عمي طرشك؟ أنا ما سويت شي، كانت مزحة
ʿammi ṭarrashak? ana ma sawwēt shay, kānat mazḥa
Did my uncle send you? I didn't do anything; it was a joke.
B
عمك كلمني. بس راشد انفضح قدام الكل
ʿammak kallamni. bas Rāshid infaẓaḥ jiddām il-kill
Your uncle talked to me. But Rāshid was shown up in front of everyone.
A
والله ما كان قصدي أكسر خاطره. بس هو رد علي قدام الأهل كلهم!
wallāh ma kān gaṣdi aksir khāṭrah. bas huwa radd ʿalay jiddām il-ahal killhum!
Honestly, I didn't mean to hurt his feelings. But he answered me back in front of the whole family!
B
أدري، وغلط. بس انت الكبير، وكسرت خاطره
adri, w ghiliṭ. bas inta l-kabīr, w kasart khāṭrah
I know, and he was wrong. But you're the older one, and you hurt his feelings.
A
وأبوي للحين زعلان. يعني راشد حاقد علي؟
w ubūy lil-ḥīn zaʿlān. yaʿni Rāshid ḥāgid ʿalay?
And my father's still upset. So Rāshid's got a grudge against me?
B
لا، قلبه أبيض. بس كل واحد راكب راسه، وصرتوا متهاوشين
la, galbah abyaẓ. bas kill wāḥid rākib rāsah, w ṣirtu mithāwshīn
No, he doesn't hold grudges. But you've both dug your heels in, and now you've fallen out.
A
زين، شو تبيني أسوي؟
zēn, shu tabīni asawwi?
OK, what do you want me to do?
B
صار سوء فهم وخلاص. امسح المقطع وابدا انت، قبل لا تكبر الفتنة
ṣār sūʼ fahm w khalāṣ. imsaḥ il-magṭaʿ w ibda inta, gabil la tikbar il-fitna
It was a misunderstanding, that's all. Delete the clip and make the first move, before the bad blood grows.
A
خلاص، اللي صار صار. وبكلم أبوي بعد. عفا الله عما سلف
khalāṣ, illi ṣār ṣār. w bakallim ubūy baʿad. ʿafa llāh ʿamma salaf
All right, what's done is done. I'll talk to my father too. Let bygones be bygones.
items: you hurt his feelings (lit. you broke his khāṭir, his spirit) (to a man)
to a woman: kasarti khāṭrah (كسرتي خاطره); I hurt his feelings: kasart khāṭrah
(he's) got a grudge against me, (he) bears me a grudge
about a woman: ḥāgda ʿalay (حاقدة علي)
he doesn't hold grudges, he's good-hearted (lit. his heart is white)
about a woman: galbha abyaẓ (قلبها أبيض)
let bygones be bygones (lit. God has pardoned what is past; from the Qurʼan)

title: Checkpoint 5.4: peace in the majlis
goal: Checkpoint: in Bū Rāshid's majlis, Rāshid and Ḥamad have made up; take his thanks, and tell him how your complaint and your apology went
tip: Recycle the block: the peace (kasar khāṭrah, sūʼ fahm, rākib rāsah, rawwig), the complaint (inghashshēt, il-masʼūl) and the apology (il-khaṭaʼ min ʿindana, ḥaṣal khēr). When an elder praises you, pass it on, with a joke if you like.
dialogue: A
شوف راشد وحمد يضحكون. رجعت المياه لمجاريها، والفضل لك يا سالم
shūf Rāshid w Ḥamad yiẓḥakūn. rijʿat il-myāh l-majārīha, w il-faẓl lak yā Sālim
Look at Rāshid and Ḥamad laughing. Things are back to normal, and it's thanks to you, Sālim.
B
الحمد لله. حمد ما كان متعمد، بس كسر خاطره، وصار سوء فهم
il-ḥamdu lillāh. Ḥamad ma kān mitʿammid, bas kasar khāṭrah, w ṣār sūʼ fahm
Thank God. Ḥamad didn't mean it, but he hurt his feelings, and there was a misunderstanding.
A
انت اللي صلحت بينهم. انت ريّال واعي ومتزن، وربيع وفي، وتكسب الناس
inta illi ṣallaḥt bēnhum. inta rayyāl wāʿi w mitzin, w rbīʿ wafi, w tiksib in-nās
You're the one who made peace between them. You're a sensible, steady man, a loyal friend, and you win people over.
B
بس هالأسبوع ما كنت واعي ولا متزن، كنت منرفز!
bas hal-usbūʿ ma kint wāʿi wala mitzin, kint mnarfaz!
But this week I wasn't sensible or steady; I was fed up!
A
منرفز؟ ليش؟ شو صار؟
mnarfaz? lēsh? shu ṣār?
Fed up? Why? What happened?
B
اللابتوب. حسيت إني انغشيت، بس المسؤول شافه وبدلوه
il-lābtōb. ḥassēt inni inghashshēt, bas il-masʼūl shāfah w baddalōh
The laptop. I felt I'd been ripped off, but the manager looked at it, and they replaced it.
A
زين. وسمعت إنك غلطت مع عميل؟
zēn. w simaʿt innak ghilaṭt maʿa ʿamīl?
Good. And I heard you made a mistake with a client?
B
قلت له: الخطأ من عندنا. وقال حصل خير
gilt-lah: il-khaṭaʼ min ʿindana. w gāl ḥaṣal khēr
I told him: the mistake was ours. And he said no harm done.
A
هذا الصح. اللي يعترف بغلطه كبير، وانت صاير قدوة لراشد
hādha ṣ-ṣaḥḥ. illi yiʿtirif b-ghalaṭah kbīr, w inta ṣāyir qudwa l-Rāshid
That's right. A man who admits his mistake is a big man, and you've become a role model for Rāshid.
B
قدوة؟ لا يا عمي. بس إذا راشد ركب راسه مرة ثانية، بقول له: روق!
qudwa? la yā ʿammi. bas idha Rāshid rikab rāsah marra thānya, bagūl-lah: rawwig!
A role model? No, uncle. But if Rāshid digs his heels in again, I'll tell him: chill!
items: things are back to normal (lit. the waters are back in their channels)
you win people over (to a man)
to a woman: tiksbīn in-nās (تكسبين الناس); (recognise)
steady, composed, keeping your head (a man)

title: When the sea fed everyone
goal: In Bū Rāshid's majlis, with Rāshid there, ask about his grandfather, a pearl diver, and what life at sea was like before oil
tip: Old words come with the old stories: nōkhidha, sēb. Just recognise them. To keep an elder talking, ask short follow-ups (w cham shahar?, shu shughulhum biẓ-ẓabṭ?) and react (subḥān allāh).
grammar: heritage I: asking an elder about the old days (w cham…?, shu shughulhum?)
dialogue: A
يدي، الله يرحمه، كان غواص، وكان ولد حلال. من وهو صغير في البحر
yaddi, allāh yirḥamah, kān ghawwāṣ, w kān wild ḥalāl. min w huwa ṣghīr fi l-baḥar
My grandfather, God rest him, was a pearl diver, and a decent man. He was at sea from when he was little.
B
آمين، الله يرحمه. يعني كان يغوص على اللولو؟
āmīn, allāh yirḥamah. yaʿni kān yighūṣ ʿala l-lūlu?
Amen, God rest him. So he dived for pearls?
A
هيه، قبل النفط، الناس رزقهم كله من البحر
hē, gabil in-nafṭ, in-nās rizg-hum killah min il-baḥar
Yes; before oil, people's whole living came from the sea.
B
وكم شهر كانوا يقعدون في البحر؟
w cham shahar kānaw yigʿdūn fi l-baḥar?
And how many months did they stay at sea?
A
في الغوص الكبير، الصيف كله تقريبا. والنوخذة هو المسؤول عن كل شي
fi l-ghōṣ il-kbīr, iṣ-ṣēf killah tagrīban. w in-nōkhidha huwa l-masʼūl ʿan kill shay
In the big dive, almost the whole summer. And the nōkhidha was in charge of everything.
B
ومنو غيرهم كان في السفينة؟ شو شغلهم بالضبط؟
w minu ghērhum kān fi s-safīna? shu shughulhum biẓ-ẓabṭ?
And who else was on the boat? What were their jobs, exactly?
A
في السيب، يمسك الحبل، وإذا الغواص حركه، يسحبه فوق
fī s-sēb, yimsik il-ḥabil, w idha l-ghawwāṣ ḥarrakah, yisḥabah fōg
There was the sēb: he held the rope, and when the diver tugged it, he pulled him up.
B
وكم يقدر الغواص يكتم نفسه تحت الماي؟
w cham yigdar il-ghawwāṣ yiktim nafasah taḥt il-māy?
And how long can a diver hold his breath under water?
A
يدي كان يقول دقيقتين، وأحيانا أكثر. كانت حياة صعبة، بس كان رزين، متزن، ما يشتكي
yaddi kān ygūl digīgtēn, w aḥyānan akthar. kānat ḥayā ṣaʿba, bas kān rizīn, mitzin, ma yishtiki
My grandfather used to say two minutes, sometimes more. It was a hard life, but he was steady and composed, and never complained.
B
سبحان الله، يدك قدوة. وأنا أتعب من نص ساعة في المسبح!
subḥān allāh, yaddak qudwa. w ana atʿab min nuṣṣ sāʿa fi l-masbaḥ!
Glory be to God; your grandfather's an example. And I get tired after half an hour in the pool!
items: the captain (who ran the pearling boat and shared out the earnings)
the rope man (who lowered the diver and pulled him up)
their living, what they lived on (lit. their provision from God)
I hold my breath: aktim nafasi (أكتم نفسي)
culture: Before oil, pearl diving was one of the main trades of the Emirates. The main season, il-ghōṣ il-kbīr ('the big dive'), ran from early June to the end of September. The nōkhidha owned the boat or ran it for its owner, and shared out the season's earnings; the sēb handled the ropes that lowered the divers and pulled them up when they tugged.
task: This week: search YouTube for «قصص الغوص» (pearl-diving stories) or «الغوص على اللؤلؤ». Find an older speaker telling his own memories and listen for 10 minutes. Within a minute you should hear شو / مب; if you hear سوف or ليس all the time, pick another clip. Note every word from this week's lessons you hear (in-nōkhidha, is-sēb, rizg) with the sentence around it.

title: Not every oyster has a pearl
goal: At a heritage stall in Shindagha, an old man whose father was a diver shows you and Mājid a diver's tools; ask what they're made of and what each one was for
tip: Asking about an object: min shu msawwa? 'what's it made of?' and w hādhi, shu fāyidt-ha? 'and what's this one for?'. Heritage words (fiṭām, ḥaṣāt il-ghōṣ, hērāt) are for recognising.
grammar: heritage I: asking about old objects (min shu msawwa?, shu fāyidt-ha?)
dialogue: A
هذا الفطام. الغواص يحطه على خشمه، عشان ما يدخل الماي
hādha l-fiṭām. il-ghawwāṣ yḥuṭṭah ʿala khashmah, ʿashān ma yidkhil il-māy
This is the fiṭām. The diver put it on his nose, so the water wouldn't get in.
B
ما شاء الله، صغير وايد. من شو مسوى؟
mā shāʼ allāh, ṣghīr wāyid. min shu msawwa?
Goodness, it's tiny. What's it made of?
A
من العظم. والسيب ماسك الحبل، والغواص ينزل وهو يكتم نفسه
min il-ʿaẓum. w is-sēb māsik il-ḥabil, w il-ghawwāṣ yinzil w huwa yiktim nafasah
Bone. The sēb held the rope, and the diver went down holding his breath.
B
وهذي، شو فايدتها؟
w hādhi, shu fāyidt-ha?
And this one, what's it for?
A
هذي حصاة الغوص، يربطها في ريله عشان ينزل. وتحت يلقى المحار في الهيرات
hādhi ḥaṣāt il-ghōṣ, yarbuṭha fi rīlah ʿashān yinzil. w taḥt yilga l-maḥār fi l-hērāt
This is the diving stone; he tied it to his foot so he'd sink. And down there he found the oysters in the hērāt, the pearl beds.
B
وكلها فيها لولو؟
w killha fīha lūlu?
And do they all have pearls in them?
A
اسمعني يا ولدي، يفتحون مية محارة، ويمكن ما يلقون ولا وحدة
ismaʿni yā wildi, yiftaḥūn miyat maḥāra, w yimkin ma yilgūn wala waḥda
Listen to me, son: they'd open a hundred oysters and maybe not find a single one.
B
يعني اللولو نادر، وكان رزقهم على الله
yaʿni l-lūlu nādir, w kān rizg-hum ʿala llāh
So pearls are rare, and their living was in God's hands.
A
هيه. وإذا لقوا وحدة كبيرة نادرة، النوخذة يستانس قبل الكل
hē. w idha ligaw waḥda kbīra nādra, in-nōkhidha yistānis gabl il-kill
Yes. And if they found a big, rare one, the nōkhidha was the happiest of all.
B
ماجد، صور هالأشيا. أبي أطرش الصور لسيف
Mājid, ṣawwir hal-ashya. abi aṭarrish iṣ-ṣuwar l-Sēf
Mājid, take a photo of these things. I want to send the pictures to Sēf.
items: the nose clip (a pearl diver's, made of bone)
the diving stone (a weight tied to the diver's foot)
the pearl beds, the oyster banks

title: Across the Creek by abra
goal: With Bū Rāshid and Rāshid, cross Dubai Creek on an abra to Deira, and ask about the big wooden dhows moored on the other side
tip: When you ask about how things were made, Gulf speech uses simple patterns: min khashab 'of wood', bil-īd 'by hand', lōḥ lōḥ 'plank by plank'. Old trade words (maḥāmil, galāfa) are for recognising.
grammar: heritage I: how things were made and used (min khashab, bil-īd)
dialogue: A
يلا يا شباب، بنركب العبرة لديرة. أحسن من الزحمة
yalla yā shabāb, binirkab il-ʿabra l-Dēra. aḥsan min iz-zaḥma
Come on, lads, we'll take the abra to Deira. Better than the traffic.
B
أول مرة أركب عبرة! كلها من خشب؟
awwal marra arkab ʿabra! killha min khashab?
It's my first time on an abra! Is it all wood?
A
هيه. والعبرة من زمان توصل الناس من بر دبي لديرة، على الخور
hē. w il-ʿabra min zamān twaṣṣil in-nās min Bur Dbayy l-Dēra, ʿala l-khōr
Yes. The abra has taken people from Bur Dubai to Deira across the Creek for ages.
B
والخور كان جي زحمة قبل النفط؟
w il-khōr kān chī zaḥma gabil in-nafṭ?
And was the Creek this busy before oil?
A
كان فيه المحامل. هذيلا اللي هناك، كانت تسافر الهند وأفريقيا، وفيها رزقهم
kān fīh il-maḥāmil. hādhēla illi hnāk, kānat tsāfir il-hind w afrīqya, w fīha rizg-hum
There were the big wooden ships. Those ones over there used to sail to India and Africa, and people's living was in them.
B
ما شاء الله، كبيرة! وكانوا يسوونها بالإيد؟ هذا شي نادر
mā shāʼ allāh, kbīra! w kānaw ysawwūnha bil-īd? hādha shay nādir
Goodness, they're big! And they built them by hand? That's rare.
A
اسمعني، هذي القلافة. القلاف يبنيه لوح لوح، شهور
ismaʿni, hādhi l-galāfa. il-gallāf yibnīh lōḥ lōḥ, shhūr
Listen: that's galāfa. The shipwright built it plank by plank, for months.
B
وانت يا عمي، سافرت في وحدة منها؟
w inta yā ʿammi, sāfart fi waḥda minha?
And you, uncle, have you sailed on one?
A
مرة وحدة، وأنا صغير. وراشد؟ هذا ما يركب إلا البلايستيشن!
marra waḥda, w ana ṣghīr. w Rāshid? hādha ma yirkab illa l-blēstēshin!
Once, when I was little. And Rāshid? The only thing he rides is the PlayStation!
B
حرام عليك يا عمي! بس يمكن صح
ḥarām ʿalēk yā ʿammi! bas yimkin ṣaḥḥ
That's not fair, uncle! But maybe it's true.
items: we'll take the abra (the small wooden boat that crosses Dubai Creek)
the Creek (Dubai Creek); a sea inlet
the big wooden ships, the dhows; one ship: maḥmal
dhow-building, the craft of building wooden ships
culture: The abra, a small wooden boat, is one of Dubai's oldest forms of public transport: it still crosses Dubai Creek between Deira and Bur Dubai, and its name comes from ʿabar 'to cross'. il-galāfa, the old craft of building wooden ships (maḥāmil), made the boats that traded with India and the coast of East Africa.

title: Lanes, towers and palm fronds
goal: On a Friday walk in Al Fahidi with your classmate Khalfān, ask how the old houses were built and how people kept cool
tip: Talk about how things used to be with kānaw + present: kānaw yibnūn bil-ḥajar 'they used to build with stone', kānaw yiskinūn fi ʿarīsh. Khalfān's old words (sikīk, ʿarīsh, jarīd in-nakhal) are for recognising.
grammar: heritage I: how things used to be (kānaw yibnūn…, kānaw yiskinūn…)
dialogue: A
هذا الفهيدي، يم الخور. شوف البراجيل فوق البيوت
hādha l-Fahīdi, yamm il-khōr. shūf il-barājīl fōg il-byūt
This is Al Fahidi, by the Creek. Look at the wind towers on top of the houses.
B
أعرفها، تيب الهوا للبيت قبل النفط والمكيفات. وهالبيوت من شو؟
aʿarfha, tyīb il-hawa lil-bēt gabil in-nafṭ w il-mkayyifāt. w hal-byūt min shu?
I know them; they bring the air into the house, before oil and air conditioning. And what are these houses made of?
A
كانوا يبنون بالحجر والجص، والسقف من خشب
kānaw yibnūn bil-ḥajar w il-jiṣṣ, w is-sagf min khashab
They used to build with stone and gypsum, and the roof was wood.
B
والطرق ضيقة وتلف وايد. أحس إني بضيع!
w iṭ-ṭurug ẓayyga w tliff wāyid. aḥiss inni baẓīʿ!
And the lanes are narrow and twist a lot. I feel I'm going to get lost!
A
هذي السكيك. الحين فيها معارض ومتاحف، بس أول كانت بيوت ناس
hādhi s-sikīk. il-ḥīn fīha maʿāriẓ w matāḥif, bas awwal kānat byūt nās
These are the old lanes. Now there are galleries and museums here, but before they were people's homes.
B
وليش الدرايش قليلة على الشارع؟
w lēsh id-darāyish qalīla ʿala sh-shāriʿ?
And why are there so few windows on the street?
A
عشان الخصوصية. وفي الصيف، وايد ناس كانوا يسكنون في عريش
ʿashān il-khuṣūṣiyya. w fi ṣ-ṣēf, wāyid nās kānaw yiskinūn fi ʿarīsh
For privacy. And in summer, lots of people used to live in an ʿarīsh.
B
يعني بيت صغير من النخل؟
yaʿni bēt ṣghīr min in-nakhal?
You mean a little house made of palm?
A
هيه، من جريد النخل. الهوا يدخل من بينه، يدتي تقول كان أبرد من بيوتنا
hē, min jarīd in-nakhal. il-hawa yidkhil min bēnah, yaddti tgūl kān abrad min byūtna
Yes, of palm fronds. The air comes in between them; my grandma says it was cooler than our houses.
B
ما أصدق! يلا، نشرب كرك ونكمل
ma aṣaddig! yalla, nishrab karak w nkammil
I can't believe it! Come on, let's have a karak and carry on.
items: the (old, narrow) lanes, the alleys; one lane: sikka
an ʿarīsh, a summer house of palm fronds
culture: Al Fahidi, by Dubai Creek, keeps the look of Dubai from the mid-19th century to the 1970s: houses of stone, gypsum, teak and palm wood, tall wind towers (barājīl), few front windows for privacy, and winding lanes. Today its houses hold galleries and museums. In summer, many families lived in an ʿarīsh, a house of palm fronds that let the air through.

title: Freej: the old neighbourhood
goal: At the office lunch with the team, Maryam talks about the cartoon Freej and her grandmother's neighbourhood; ask her what life in the frīj was like
tip: Compare then and now with awwal … and kānaw + verb, against il-ḥīn …: awwal il-kill yaʿarf il-kill, kānaw ywazzʿūn ʿala l-jīrān, w il-ḥīn kill wāḥid mnʿazil. With Maryam, keep your -ich and -īn: yaddtich, taʿarfīn.
grammar: comparing then and now (awwal …, kānaw + verb, w il-ḥīn …)
dialogue: A
شفتوا فريج؟ الكرتون حق الأربع يدات اللي يسولفون طول اليوم
shiftu Firīj? il-kartūn ḥagg il-arbaʿ yaddāt illi ysōlfūn ṭūl il-yōm
Have you all seen Freej? The cartoon about the four grannies who chat all day.
B
هيه، أم خماس! يدتج كانت جي؟
hē, Umm Khammās! yaddtich kānat chī?
Yes, Umm Khammās! Was your grandmother like that?
A
بالضبط. كانت ساكنة في الشندغة قبل النفط، وفي الصيف في عريش. للحين تقول للرز والسكر المير
biẓ-ẓabṭ. kānat sākna fi sh-Shindagha gabil in-nafṭ, w fi ṣ-ṣēf fi ʿarīsh. lil-ḥīn tgūl lir-rizz w is-sikkar il-mīr
Exactly. She lived in Shindagha before oil, and in an ʿarīsh in summer. She still calls rice and sugar il-mīr.
B
وشو كان يصير في الفريج؟ تذكرين سوالفها؟
w shu kān yṣīr fi l-firīj? tidhkrīn sawālifha?
And what went on in the frīj? Do you remember her stories?
A
تقول أول الكل يعرف الكل، والعيال كانوا يلعبون في السكيك، والكل يتفقد الثاني
tgūl awwal il-kill yaʿarf il-kill, w il-ʿyāl kānaw yilʿabūn fi s-sikīk, w il-kill yitfaggad ith-thāni
She says that in the old days everyone knew everyone, the kids used to play in the lanes, and everyone looked out for each other.
B
وإذا حد طبخ شي؟
w idha ḥad ṭabakh shay?
And if someone cooked something?
A
كانوا يوزعون على الجيران، والجيران يوزعون عليهم. كان في تعاون
kānaw ywazzʿūn ʿala l-jīrān, w il-jīrān ywazzʿūn ʿalēhum. kān fī taʿāwun
They'd share it out among the neighbours, and the neighbours did the same for them. People helped each other.
B
والحين؟ تعرفين جيرانج؟
w il-ḥīn? taʿarfīn jīrānich?
And now? Do you know your neighbours?
A
بصراحة لا. الحين كل واحد منعزل في بيته
b-ṣarāḥa la. il-ḥīn kill wāḥid mnʿazil fi bētah
Honestly, no. Now everyone keeps to himself in his own house.
B
يا حسافة. حتى أنا، ما أعرف منو ساكن يمي في مردف!
yā ḥasāfa. ḥatta ana, ma aʿarf minu sākin yammi fi Mirdif!
What a shame. Even me: I don't know who lives next door to me in Mirdif!
items: what a shame, what a pity
they share out, they hand out
cut off, keeping to himself, isolated (a man)
he checks on, he looks in on (someone)
culture: Freej, an Emirati computer-animated cartoon first shown in Ramadan 2006, follows four grandmothers in Dubai: Umm Khammās, Umm Salūm, Umm Saʿīd and Umm ʿAllāwi. firīj is the Emirati word for neighbourhood.

title: The singer on the boat
goal: On a video call from abroad, Sēf hears you've been learning about pearling; tell him what you learnt, and hear what his grandmother told him
tip: Retelling for a friend: start from the big picture (gabil in-nafṭ…), give one detail that surprised you, and link old and new (it-turāth, il-māẓi). Sēf's old words (nahhām, tabbāb, sardāl, ahāzīj) are for recognising.
grammar: retelling what you've learnt (gabil in-nafṭ…, ma kint adri)
dialogue: A
ها يا سالم! عمي يقول صرت تعرف عن الغوص أكثر منا!
hā yā Sālim! ʿammi ygūl ṣirt taʿarf ʿan il-ghōṣ akthar minna!
Hey, Sālim! My uncle says you know more about pearling than us now!
B
لا تبالغ! بس عمك علمني وايد عن التراث
la tbālig! bas ʿammak ʿallamni wāyid ʿan it-turāth
Don't exaggerate! But your uncle taught me a lot about the heritage.
A
يلا، قول لي باختصار
yalla, gūl-li b-ikhtiṣār
Go on, tell me in short.
B
قبل النفط، رزق الناس كان من البحر، من اللولو والسمك
gabil in-nafṭ, rizg in-nās kān min il-baḥar, min il-lūlu w is-simach
Before oil, people's living came from the sea, from pearls and fish.
A
صح. ويدتي تقول كان في كل محمل نهام، يغني الأهازيج للبحارة
ṣaḥḥ. w yaddti tgūl kān fi kill maḥmal nahhām, yghanni l-ahāzīj lil-baḥḥāra
Right. And my grandma says every ship had a nahhām, who sang the old chants for the crew.
B
يغني؟ وهم يشتغلون؟ ما كنت أدري
yghanni? w hum yishtaghlūn? ma kint adri
He sang? While they worked? I had no idea.
A
هيه، عشان ينسون التعب. والتباب، عيال صغار يساعدون السيب. والسردال يقود كل السفن
hē, ʿashān yinsūn it-taʿab. w it-tabbāb, ʿyāl ṣghār ysāʿdūn is-sēb. w is-sardāl ygūd kill is-sufun
Yes, so they'd forget how tired they were. The tabbāb, young boys, helped the rope man. And the sardāl led the whole fleet.
B
عيال صغار في البحر؟ الماضي كان صعب وايد
ʿyāl ṣghār fi l-baḥar? il-māẓi kān ṣaʿb wāyid
Young boys at sea? The past was really hard.
A
والله صرت خبير! لما أرجع، بنركب العبرة سوا وتشرح لي
wallāh ṣirt khabīr! lamma arjaʿ, binirkab il-ʿabra sawa w tishraḥ-li
Honestly, you're an expert now! When I'm back, we'll take the abra together and you can explain it all to me.
B
اتفقنا. بس انت اللي بتعزمني على الكرك!
ittafagna. bas inta illi bitʿazimni ʿala l-karak!
Deal. But you're the one buying the karak!
items: the fleet captain (who led all the pearling boats)
the singer on a pearling boat (who led the crew's chants)
the (sailors') chants, the old work songs
the boys (about 10 to 14) who helped haul the divers up
task: This week: with a tutor or exchange partner, talk for 10 minutes about life before oil in the Gulf, or in their own grandparents' time: what work people did and what was hard. Use gabil in-nafṭ, rizg-hum and il-māẓi. Then give the same story for 2 minutes as if in Bū Rāshid's majlis: respectful, no English, and end by asking an elder's question: shu tidhkur min ayyām awwal?
